unit.title: Parse a tag list without the split traps
Bug hunt: parse a tag list without the split traps

fund-java/02-strings-and-immutability/01.instructions:
**Skills:** split · LinkedHashSet  
**Level:** ★☆☆

**Interview prompt.** "Users type tags like ` ,Java,  spring ,java,,SQL ` into one box. Store a clean, deduplicated, lower-case list."

**Why it matters.** `split` takes a regex, produces a leading empty string when the input starts with a separator, and case conversion depends on the locale. A tag parser hits all three.

**Your task.** Implement `static List<String> parseTags(String raw)`:
- tags are separated by commas and/or whitespace (any mix and amount)
- each tag is lower-cased with `Locale.ROOT`
- empty pieces are dropped
- duplicates are removed, keeping the FIRST occurrence's position
- other characters (including `.` and `-`) are part of the tag
- `null` or blank input gives an empty list

**Worked example.** `parseTags(" ,Java,  spring ,java,,SQL ")` is `[java, spring, sql]`.
hints: One regular expression can describe "one or more commas or whitespace characters".
Split on any run of commas or whitespace, drop the empty pieces, lower-case with a fixed locale, and keep only the first occurrence of each tag, in the order seen.
Break the text wherever commas or spaces appear, ignore empty pieces, normalise each tag's case with the root locale, and keep only the first time each tag appears, in the order seen.

fund-java/02-strings-and-immutability/02.instructions:
**Skills:** debugging · split · LinkedHashSet  
**Level:** ★☆☆

**Bug hunt.** The code in the editor is a plausible first attempt at drill 1, "Parse a tag list without the split traps". It passes some of the tests, but it has one real bug, the kind a reviewer should catch before it ships.

**Your task.** Find the bug and fix it, changing as little as you can; the tests are the same as drill 1's. The spec is unchanged: Implement `static List<String> parseTags(String raw)`:
- tags are separated by commas and/or whitespace (any mix and amount)
- each tag is lower-cased with `Locale.ROOT`
- empty pieces are dropped
- duplicates are removed, keeping the FIRST occurrence's position
- other characters (including `.` and `-`) are part of the tag
- `null` or blank input gives an empty list
fund-java/02-strings-and-immutability/02.explanation:
The planted bug is the missing empty-piece check. A leading separator makes `split("[,\\s]+")` return an empty first element, and without the `isEmpty` check that `""` is added as a tag. So "messy input becomes a clean list" fails: its input starts with a space and a comma. The other four tests pass, because none of their inputs starts with a separator (an input of only separators splits into no pieces at all). The fix is one condition, not a new regex:

```java
if (!piece.isEmpty()) seen.add(piece.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT));
```

The `LinkedHashSet` already keeps first-seen order and removes duplicates, and the `Locale.ROOT` lower-casing is already right, so leave both as they are.
hints: Parse " , java, Spring" and print every tag with quotes around it.
When the input starts with a separator, split returns an empty first piece.
Skip pieces that are empty before adding them to the set.
